frontier.hypothesis: `move s1,zero` can be emitted LAST in the entry block (target's slot) while keeping the long live range that wins the 15000/15000 allocation tie, by giving its destination reg_n_sets == 1 so sched1's birthing boost sinks it regardless of INSN_LUID.
frontier.mechanism: rank_for_schedule falls through to a DESCENDING INSN_LUID sort for insns with no consumer in the block, so the hoisted zero-init (low LUID) is emitted first. adjust_priority()/birthing_insn_p() overrides LUID entirely when reg_n_sets[dest] == 1 - the same lever that HURT the s9 pointer split, used here in the direction that helps. The naive spelling (a separate single-set local copied into the counter, rejected/s10-zero-init-split-single-set-pseudo.c) does sink the insn but perturbs both live lengths and loses the tie at 13, so the spelling must leave the counter's own live range intact.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate spellings where the value 0 reaches the counter through a pseudo written exactly once that dies immediately, without adding an allocno that changes either live length - e.g. the zero sourced from a once-written local whose live range sits entirely in the pre-call region, or an ordering where the counter's first WRITE is the entry increment and the 0 arrives on the not-taken path. Measure each with tools/ra_solver/extract.py (both pris must stay at 15000, or the pointer must be strictly above) AND check the block-0 ready list in tmp/grind/func_80037A20/dumps/code6cac_c.sched for a `(7f...)` boost on the zero-init insn.

frontier.hypothesis: A byte-free way to lengthen the counter's live range or shorten the pointer's that does NOT depend on the zero-init's source position decouples the allocation from the schedule, letting the zero-init keep a late (target) source position.
frontier.mechanism: The allocation currently rides on statement position because that is the only live-length lever s10 found. Any other perturbation that moves ptr livelen 17 -> 16 (or the counter 14 -> 20) leaves the zero-init free to sit after the sprintf call, where its high INSN_LUID emits it last in the block exactly as target does.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep loop-shape and tail-shape variants of the ONE-POINTER body with the zero-init AFTER the call, reading tools/ra_solver/extract.py after each: loop-exit spelling (goto end vs fallthrough), where the -1 compensation sits, the position of the gp store relative to the return, and whether the nextfile result is consumed in the while-condition versus a named temp. Target is ptr pri >= counter pri at 33 insns.

frontier.hypothesis: The entry-increment fold (`li $s1,1` vs target `addiu $s1,$s1,1`) closes for free once the schedule is fixed, because on this chassis it is not independently attackable.
frontier.mechanism: s6 pinned the fold to the FIRST cse.c pass (REG_WAS_0 note on the dominating zero-init). Every s10 attempt to break it either failed to break it or cost the allocation tie, which suggests the fold and the tie are two readings of the same live-range balance rather than independent levers.
frontier.next_probe: After (and only after) the schedule frontier above lands, re-measure the fold on whatever body wins: if the zero-init ends up sunk by the birthing boost, first grep REG_WAS_0 in the func_80037A20 region of tmp/grind/func_80037A20/dumps/code6cac_c.cse to see whether cse1 still attaches the note at all, before spending any spelling attempts on it.
